title: DigitalOcean Managed Agents Brings Managed Cloud Infrastructure to AI Agents
gist: DigitalOcean launched Managed Agents in public preview, pairing a microVM Harness Runtime (pause/resume/fork sessions) with an MCP-based Action Gateway (16,000+ tools, permissions, human approval). It overlaps with Docker's Cloud Sandboxes but targets production orchestration.

insights.claim: DigitalOcean launched Managed Agents in public preview, a managed cloud layer for AI agents combining isolated microVM runtimes, governed tool access and serverless AI inference.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Cloud providers are moving up the stack from VMs to agent-specific platforms; watch DigitalOcean's agent adoption.

insights.claim: DigitalOcean argues agentic workflows differ from traditional cloud apps, and developers running agents on conventional VMs must build the runtime plumbing themselves: context preservation, artifact persistence, parallel coordination and hardened tool access.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: The pitch is that undifferentiated agent plumbing is a monetizable managed-service layer.
insights.quote: Developers are forced to invest in plumbing work to preserve the agent's context
insights.locator: According to DigitalOcean, agentic workflows differ

insights.claim: Running agents on plain VMs also requires keeping spare VM capacity so agents start quickly and provisioning compute on demand, costs that a managed service aims to absorb.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Idle-capacity overhead is a cost argument for managed agent runtimes.
insights.locator: Further challenges include maintaining spare VM capacity

insights.claim: The product has two integrated services, a Harness Runtime and an Action Gateway, with DigitalOcean managing execution, persistence, tool access and underlying infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Runtime plus governed tool gateway is a template for how agent platforms are being packaged.

insights.claim: The Harness Runtime is built on lightweight microVMs and supports multiple harnesses: Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Hermes, and custom LangGraph agents.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Harness-agnostic hosting positions DigitalOcean as neutral infrastructure across competing coding agents.

insights.claim: Sessions persist conversational history and working state and can be paused, resumed or forked, and agents are automatically paused when idle, meaning no ongoing LLM or tool calls.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Pause-when-idle lowers compute cost for bursty agent workloads, a key unit-economics lever.
insights.locator: The harness runtime can persist conversational history

insights.claim: Sessions run on security-hardened compute and storage, can reach internal services without public exposure, and can be launched in parallel across repositories and tasks for divide-and-conquer, collaboration and map/reduce workflows.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Parallel isolated sessions are the scaling primitive for agentic coding workloads.
insights.locator: Each session runs on security-hardened compute

insights.claim: The Action Gateway exposes a unified MCP endpoint with more than 16,000 tools, including web search, web fetch, browser automation, DigitalOcean infrastructure APIs, and connectors for GitHub, HubSpot and Stripe.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: MCP is becoming the de facto tool-access standard; a broad connector catalog is a platform moat.
insights.locator: The Action Gateway is the agent's interface

insights.claim: The gateway centralizes permission management over which tools and actions each agent may use, requires human approval for sensitive operations, and provides rate limiting, retries, backoff and timeouts for multi-agent access to external systems.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Governance and human-in-the-loop controls are enterprise buying criteria for agent deployment.
insights.locator: The gateway implements several security measures

insights.claim: Dair.ai's Elvis Saravia praised the focus on performance and cost reduction, saying many other agent management platforms are cost-prohibitive and hard to scale in production.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Cost is seen as the main barrier to production agent scaling; price-competitive platforms may win share.
insights.quote: many other agent management platforms are cost-prohibitive and make it hard to scale agents in production
insights.locator: Commenting on the announcement on X.com

insights.claim: Seaotter founder Ryan Martin described pause-when-idle plus governed tools as the operations pattern that scales for agents.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Signals emerging consensus on idle-pause and governed tooling as best practice.
insights.quote: Pause-when-idle + governed tools is the ops pattern that scales

insights.claim: Docker's Cloud Sandboxes launched around the same time with significant overlap, both offering microVM isolation and persistence; Docker focuses on developer workflows such as moving a sandbox between local and cloud, while DigitalOcean targets production infrastructure with more orchestration and tool support.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Agent sandbox/runtime is becoming a contested category; differentiation is dev workflow versus production orchestration.
insights.locator: DigitalOcean Managed Agents arrive around the same time
